about: Known SQLite bugs: the one list build-clis.sh, pretriage.py and the nightly check read. Paths are relative to the repository root. fix: the patch against a fresh trunk tree (https://sqlite.org/src/tarball/trunk/sqlite.tar.gz), applied as `patch -p<strip> -d <tree>/<dir> -i <path>`; null when there is none (then `match` says how a finding is recognized). repro: a self-contained SQL file run as `sqlite3 -batch -init /dev/null :memory: < repro` (stdout and stderr together); expected: its exact output on a correct build (generated from the patched CLI). status: open, or fixed once trunk has the fix: then build-clis.sh, pre-triage and the nightly check pass it over, and fixed_in records the fix (its check-in, how it reached trunk, the trunk it was checked on); the entry stays, as the record (pretriage.py --check-bugs lists them as retired). A bug without a fix has fix null and match: error (null for a wrong result), sql_all and sql_any patterns.

bugs.name: sqlite-overflow-text-bom
bugs.summary: In a UTF-16 database, a TEXT value over 4000 bytes read from a table's overflow pages loses a leading U+FEFF (a leading U+FFFE flips the rest's byte order): vdbeColumnFromOverflow's RCStr text path passes the database encoding to sqlite3VdbeMemSetStr, which handles a BOM; table and index disagree, integrity_check reports a missing index row (reported, bug forum 36a73e8c8a)

fixed_in.how: drh, 2026-10-16 18:11: "Fix a problem with reading large UTF16 strings with a BOM out of the VDBE column cache. Bug 2026-10-13T01:16:49Z" (our bug-forum report 36a73e8c8a); check.sql prints its expected output on trunk 5bd093e261a7, where our fix.diff no longer applies

bugs.name: sqlite-propagate-const-real-minint
bugs.summary: WHERE b = -9223372036854775808.0 AND typeof(b) = 'integer' (or a text use of b) missed a row whose INT column b holds the INTEGER -2^63, and a stored REAL -2^63 the other way round: constant propagation codes the constant plus OP_Affinity, which left REAL -2^63 a REAL (since 3.25.0 with a join, 3.36.0 on one table; not reported). Upstream's bFromText change (sqlite3VdbeIntegerAffinity converts REAL -2^63 to INTEGER unless from text; between 3769f60be38b and 03f699544e6b) fixed the INTEGER direction (check q1, q2, q4); still open for a REAL -2^63 stored in an INT/NUMERIC column (from the text '-9223372036854775808.0' or an older database): `b = -9223372036854775808 AND typeof(b) = 'real'` misses it (q3). The check is check-v2.sql (q3 inserts the text, since 03f699544e6b stores the REAL literal as INTEGER): 3769f60be38b 0 0 0 0, 03f699544e6b 1 1 0 1. Our own fix (fix-trunk.diff, 2026-10-16) for the fixed target; not upstream.

match.how: no fix to test, and a wrong result, not an error: a reproduced failure is this bug when its SQL compares a column with the REAL constant -9223372036854775808.0 (written -9.223372036854776e18) and uses the same column under typeof() or as text (||, CAST AS TEXT, a text function, LIKE or GLOB), in either order (one of sql_any)

bugs.name: sqlite-in-select-collate-index
bugs.summary: x IN (SELECT y COLLATE <seq> ...) on a column x with a BINARY index seeks the index under BINARY and misses rows equal under the subquery's collating sequence (datatype3.html 7.1 says IN compares like x = y), while a scan and the expression in the select list use it: indexInAffinityOk pairs a row-value field with the subquery column but a scalar left side only with itself (every release tried, 3.28.0 to trunk; found from run 20261013-1959 tlp-where w3-63694, again as run 20261014-0121 plans-noindex w2-80173)

fixed_in.how: dan on trunk 2026-10-14 (bug forum f505c400cf)

bugs.name: sqlite-alter-default-blob-encoding
bugs.summary: In a UTF-16 database, a column added by ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with a blob DEFAULT reads that default, for rows written before the ALTER, as UTF-8 when cast to text (unicode, upper, LIKE, min see the wrong characters) unless the value passed through a sorter: valueFromExpr's TK_BLOB branch sets enc UTF-8 and OP_Column's default path never resets it (3.20.0 to trunk at least; found as run 20261014-1340 order-multiset w2-13884, plans-index-expr w1-45145, plans-noindex w2-33749)

fixed_in.how: drh on trunk 2026-10-15 (bug forum a9c654a346)

bugs.name: sqlite-gencol-index-real-int
bugs.summary: An index on a VIRTUAL generated column with no declared type (or BLOB) over a REAL column stores an integral REAL as an INTEGER and never converts it back, so reads through the index give 1|integer where the table gives 1.0|real: sqlite3GenerateIndexKey deletes the trailing OP_RealAffinity, which belongs to the REAL column inside the generation expression (3.31.0 to trunk; found as run 20261014-1340 tlp-where w0-41784 and w7-31893)

fixed_in.how: drh on trunk 2026-10-14 (bug forum 6973ad169e)

bugs.name: sqlite-wr-bignull-added-column
bugs.summary: On a WITHOUT ROWID table, ORDER BY <column added by ALTER TABLE> NULLS LAST with the primary key constrained by an IN of 2+ values seeks on a column outside the key (WHERE_BIGNULL_SORT); rows written before the ALTER lack the field: "database disk image is malformed" for a REAL or TEXT key, dropped or repeated rows for an integer key. wherePathSatisfiesOrderBy matches the NULLS LAST term past nKeyCol of the PK index (3.30.0 to trunk; found as run 20261014-2000 plans-index w1-27841)

fixed_in.how: dan on trunk 2026-10-15 (bug forum eee345f931)

bugs.name: sqlite-group-concat-inverse-empty-text
bugs.summary: group_concat()/string_agg() as a window over a moving frame (ROWS/RANGE/GROUPS with a moving start) loses the separator, then text, after an inverse step leaves the accumulated text empty while terms remain (an empty string left in the frame): groupConcatInverse resets mxAlloc (= 'first term' in groupConcatStep) on str.nChar==0 instead of nAccum==0, so the next step writes no separator and the next inverse cuts nFirstSepLength bytes off the following value (3.25.0 to trunk; found as round windows-rowvalues seed 6014 plans-noopt-WindowFunc)

fixed_in.how: dan, 2026-10-16 17:42, after the report on the bug forum (2026-10-16T15:51:51Z): "Fix a problem handling zero-length strings in some cases in group_concat() when it is used as a window function"; check.sql prints its expected output on trunk a7f6aa448f35, and build-fixed.sh found our fix.diff already in that tree
fixed_in.trunk: a7f6aa448f35

bugs.name: sqlite-wr-rowvalue-added-column
bugs.summary: On a WITHOUT ROWID table, a row-value range constraint ((pk, added) > / >= / < / <= (...)) that runs from the primary key into a column added by ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN makes the planner seek the PRIMARY KEY b-tree with that column in the key (whereRangeVectorLen caps at nColumn, not nKeyCol); rows written before the ALTER lack the field: "database disk image is malformed" on a lower bound, silently missing rows on an upper bound or an integer key. Sibling of sqlite-wr-bignull-added-column (fixed in a2a20c54a2). 3.40.0 to trunk; found as run 20261016-1540 plans-right w5-11 (RIGHT JOIN ON form)

bugs.name: sqlite-concat-blob-utf16-length
bugs.summary: In a UTF-16 database concat()/concat_ws() of a BLOB argument (or BLOB separator) copy the BLOB's size in bytes of its UTF-8 text: concatFuncCore takes sqlite3_value_bytes() before sqlite3_value_text(), so the result gets the terminator and stale bytes past it (concat(x'0041') is 'A' + NUL) or a truncated character (x'0800'); the argument is converted in place, so a constant BLOB is wrong only on the first row and table and index scans disagree. Valid UTF-16 too; no out-of-bounds read (ASAN quiet). 3.44.0 to trunk; found as query_plans_agree at fuzz 1cc3a23 (plans-index, concat(x'3f', c0)); duplicate of bug forum c621e963a9 (2026-10-16, drh: unable to reproduce)

bugs.name: sqlite-rowvalue-in-join-reuse
bugs.summary: A row-value IN ((x.a, x.b) IN (list | VALUES | SELECT)) whose first field is equated to an indexed column of an inner table (x.a = y.a / USING) drives the inner loop through the equivalence; removeUnindexableInClauseTerms drops the unused fields but keeps EP_Subrtn (cleared only when a kept field is out of place), so sqlite3CodeRhsOfIN reuses the full multi-column list (REUSE LIST SUBQUERY, OP_OpenDup) and the inner loop reads column 0 of every RHS row, duplicates included: joined rows repeated once per list element sharing the field. 3.35.0 (IN SELECT) / 3.44.0 (IN list) to trunk; found as run 20261016-1631 norec-join w9-16730 (WITHOUT ROWID self-join, (a0.c0, a0.c0) IN, after ANALYZE)

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-16 22:07: removeUnindexableInClauseTerms now clears EP_Subrtn when RHS columns were removed (our fix's change, commented 'See bug 2026-10-16T22:07:15Z'); before trunk 185ffd27064b, whose CLI prints the expected output; our fix.diff still applies (with an offset) as a duplicate of it, so it must not be applied; check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options, and on 185ffd27064b (a CLI with default options)

bugs.name: sqlite-wr-in-index-added-column
bugs.summary: On a WITHOUT ROWID table, a row-value IN / NOT IN (SELECT pk, added FROM t) whose RHS columns run from the primary key into a column added by ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN makes sqlite3FindInIndex pick the PRIMARY KEY b-tree as the IN index (it checks nColumn, not nKeyCol) and probe it with the added column in the key; rows written before the ALTER lack the field: "database disk image is malformed" for a REAL/TEXT key, NULL for an integer key, missing rows when the IN drives a loop (index cursor reads NULL, not the default). Third path after sqlite-wr-bignull-added-column (a2a20c54a2) and sqlite-wr-rowvalue-added-column. Error 3.40.0 to trunk, wrong answers from 3.20.0; found as run 20261016-1828 setops w3-29824

bugs.name: sqlite-compound-orderby-collate-groupby
bugs.summary: A UNION/EXCEPT/INTERSECT compound whose ORDER BY has a COLLATE anywhere in a term is rewritten as SELECT * FROM (compound) ORDER BY ... by convertCompoundSelectToSubquery (select.c), which clears GROUP BY and HAVING on the copied last member instead of the outer query (and keeps its SF_Distinct on the outer query): the last member's GROUP BY/HAVING/DISTINCT apply to the whole compound. "no such column" when they name a column the result lacks, wrong rows otherwise. 3.20.0 to trunk; found as plans seeds 7106 and 9640 at ephyra-sqlite ee692f5 (ORDER BY by a result column's expression containing COLLATE NOCASE)

bugs.name: sqlite-leftjoin-on-or-omitted-table-segv
bugs.summary: whereLoopAddOr lets an OR term from a LEFT JOIN's ON clause (EP_OuterON) drive a MULTI-INDEX OR loop on a table left of the join; when the LEFT JOIN table is omitted (DISTINCT, omit-noop-join), the OR branches are coded as filters on the left table (wrong rows) and a branch reading the omitted table runs OP_Column on a never-opened cursor (NULL VdbeCursor read, SIGSEGV). 3.53.2/3.53.4/3.54.0 and trunk; 3.45-3.50.4 fail with 'ON clause references tables to its right' instead (error removed by e0beda7ffe); found as run-1017 crash1.sql (DISTINCT self-join, LEFT JOIN ON (a2.c1 = a1.c0 OR a1.c0 IN (SELECT ...)))

bugs.name: sqlite-delete-saveposition-stale-cellinfo
bugs.summary: A one-pass (ONEPASS_MULTI) DELETE on a WITHOUT ROWID table deletes through a cursor with BTREE_SAVEPOSITION; when the leaf needs no rebalance sqlite3BtreeDelete (btree.c) leaves it in CURSOR_SKIPNEXT on the next cell but keeps the deleted cell's CellInfo, so a later write to the same table in the same statement (a trigger body: DELETE ... WHERE x OR pk > ..; then INSERT/UPDATE) saves that cursor via saveAllCursors -> saveCursorKey, reading the deleted key from freed page space and its freed overflow chain: "database disk image is malformed" (Overflow chain ends prematurely); the file is fine. 3.20.0 to trunk; found as run 20261017-0438 norec w3-370783 (UPDATE of a view, INSTEAD OF trigger DELETE + UPDATE, reverse_unordered_selects)

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-18; between trunk 185ffd27064b (the check prints the wrong output) and aa36cfe5b0f9 (2026-10-20 20:17) (the workspace's build-clis: build_failed): sqlite3BtreeDelete's bPreserve>1 path now zeroes pCur->info.nSize; our fix.diff's context still matches elsewhere in btree.c, where it does not compile, so it must not be applied; check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options

bugs.name: sqlite-balanced-merge-dedup-collation
bugs.summary: multiSelectByMerge (select.c) builds the duplicate-removal KeyInfo (pKeyDup) from multiSelectCollSeq of the SELECTs it is coding, not of the whole compound: the right half of a balanced merge (a UNION run of 4+ SELECTs, SQLITE_BalancedMerge) and the left operand of a merge remove duplicates under their own collation while the merge compares under the compound's. Rows equal under the part's collation but distinct under the compound's are dropped (BINARY compound, RTRIM right half: '' and ' ' become one row), and with ORDER BY a NOCASE compound keeps 'a','A' from one SELECT of its left operand. Balanced half: ORDER BY since 3.38.0, also without ORDER BY since 3.53 (plain UNION now always merges); left operand with ORDER BY: 3.20.0 to trunk. Found while fixing ephyra-sqlite's compound collation model (run 20261018-1734 setops-def w3-8985 follow-up)

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-18; between trunk 185ffd27064b (our fix.diff applies, the check prints the wrong output) and aa36cfe5b0f9 (2026-10-20 20:17) (patch_stale), with a change of its own (our fix.diff no longer applies either way); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options

bugs.name: sqlite-temp-rename-column-twice
bugs.summary: sqlite3AlterRenameColumn (alter.c) runs sqlite_rename_column over the table's own schema and then, unconditionally, over temp.sqlite_schema's triggers and views; when the table is itself in temp, every temp trigger and view is rewritten twice and the second pass resolves the already renamed text against the not yet reloaded table: ALTER TABLE <temp table> RENAME COLUMN a TO b fails with 'error in trigger tr: no such column: old.b' (or 'error in view v: no such column: b') whenever a temp trigger or view has an expression referring to the column (WHEN, NEW/OLD, SELECT, WHERE, SET RHS; not UPDATE OF / SET target / INSERT column list). RENAME TO already skips the temp pass for iDb==1. 3.25.0 to trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round attach-temp (qscore seed 4 input 1399, DROP COLUMN + RENAME COLUMN on a TEMP table with a TEMP trigger WHEN OLD.c1 ...)

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-19; before trunk 185ffd27064b (2026-10-20 13:10), whose CLI prints the expected output and where our fix.diff no longer applies (a change of its own); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options, and on 185ffd27064b (a CLI with default options)

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-eq-constprop-aux-cursor
bugs.summary: WHERE-clause constant propagation (select.c propagateConstants/constInsert) takes the FTS5 full-text term `tbl = 'query'` (documented as equal to MATCH; xBestIndex consumes it with omit=1) as COLUMN=CONSTANT and, since the hidden column's declared type 'HIDDEN' gives NUMERIC affinity, substitutes 'query' for the other references to the hidden column in WHERE, including an auxiliary function's first argument (the cursor id): `tbl = 'x' AND snippet(tbl,..)/bm25(tbl)/highlight(tbl,..) ...` fails with 'no such cursor: 0', `tbl = 'x' AND tbl = 'y'` is false, `rank = 'bm25(..)' AND rank < 0` is false. MATCH and tbl('x') forms work. 3.51.0, 3.53.4 and trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree (tlp-where over a CTE with snippet(vt0, ..))

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-match-rowid-eq-nonint
bugs.summary: fts5BestIndexMethod now sets omit for `rowid = ?` (not in 3.50.2/3.51.0), but with a MATCH fts5FilterMethod applies it only as rowid limits via fts5GetRowidLimit, which ignores anything that is not an SQLITE_INTEGER: `tbl MATCH 'q' AND rowid = <REAL, even 2.0 | non-numeric TEXT | NULL | BLOB>` returns every MATCH row (expected none, or the one row for 2.0); in a join `ft.rowid = t1.x AND ft MATCH ..` every non-integer t1.x joins all matches; `rowid IN (2.5,'x')` returns each match once per value. Integers, integer text, ranges and the no-MATCH rowid lookup are right. Regression between 3.51.0 and 3.53.2; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree (qscore seed 0 input 9828, norec-join FULL JOIN on rowid)

bugs.name: sqlite-vtab-create-rollback-to-savepoint
bugs.summary: sqlite3VtabCallCreate (vtab.c) adds a new virtual table to db->aVTrans without setting VTable.iSavepoint or calling xSavepoint (sqlite3VtabBegin then returns early for it), so a ROLLBACK TO a savepoint (inside BEGIN) that undoes the CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE never calls its xRollbackTo: FTS5/FTS4 keep the pending terms of the rolled-back INSERT and the next SAVEPOINT, CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE or COMMIT (xSavepoint/xSync flush into the dropped shadow tables) fails with 'SQL logic error'; COMMIT then rolls back the whole transaction. R-Tree unaffected; a transaction-opening SAVEPOINT unaffected. 3.51.0, 3.53.4 and trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree (qscore seed 3 input 270, setops)

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-20; between trunk 185ffd27064b (our fix applies, the check prints the wrong output) and 3769f60be38b, where our fix-v2.diff applies reversed (the same change); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-unindexed-detail-none-instances
bugs.summary: With detail=none or detail=column, fts5CsrPoslist (fts5_main.c) builds the aux-function position lists by tokenizing every column, UNINDEXED ones included, while fts5ApiColumnSize reports 0 tokens for an UNINDEXED column: snippet(tbl, -1, ..) fails with 'database disk image is malformed' (fts5SnippetFunction's io>nDocsize check) when a matched term occurs in an UNINDEXED value after its first token; highlight() of the UNINDEXED column marks the term and bm25() counts it (differs from detail=full). Integrity checks pass. 3.51.0, 3.53.4 and trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree (qscore seed 4 input 2085, seed 1 input 2499)

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-21; between trunk fa0247a431bd (16:56) and 9eafe6158d10 (20:53), with a change of its own (our fix.diff no longer applies: build-fixed.sh skipped it); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 9eafe6158d10 (2026-10-21 20:53): pretriage --check-bugs reports it fixed and the check prints its expected output on the workspace's trunk CLI

bugs.name: sqlite-geopoly-rowid-eq-nonint
bugs.summary: geopolyFilter (ext/rtree/geopoly.c) answers `rowid = ?` (omit set) with sqlite3_value_int64() of any value: `rowid = 6.5` and `rowid = '6abc'` find row 6, 'x' and NULL find rowid 0, 1e19 finds 2^63-1; `rowid IN (6.5, 7)` finds both, a LEFT JOIN on a non-integer key joins the truncated rowid, and UPDATE/DELETE .. WHERE rowid = 7.5 change row 7. R-Tree's own check (rtreeFilter) converts in the wrong order, so `id = '1e1'` misses rowid 10. One helper (rtreeRowidEqValue) fixes both. 3.46.0 to trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree-2 (qscore seed 0 input 2504, cte MATERIALIZED vs NOT MATERIALIZED)

bugs.name: sqlite-geopoly-update-rowid-nochange
bugs.summary: An UPDATE of a geopoly table that changes the rowid but not _shape fails with '_shape does not contain a valid polygon': geopolyUpdate (ext/rtree/geopoly.c) takes the bounding box and the new %_rowid row from aData[2], the unchanged (sqlite3_vtab_nochange) _shape, which is NULL; `SET rowid = 7, _shape = _shape` works. 3.46.0 to trunk; found by hand in ephyra-sqlite round rtree-geopoly

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-locale-contentless-unindexed-insert
bugs.summary: FTS5 with locale=1, content='', contentless_unindexed=1 and an UNINDEXED column: sqlite3Fts5StorageOpen (fts5_storage.c) adds an l<i> column to %_content for each indexed column, which the INSERT_CONTENT statement (it binds locales only for content=normal) does not supply, so its prepare fails and is reported as SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB: every INSERT fails with 'database disk image is malformed'. 3.50.2 to trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree-2

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-contentless-unindexed-drop-rename
bugs.summary: FTS5 content='' + contentless_unindexed=1 (with an UNINDEXED column, so a %_content table exists): sqlite3Fts5DropAll and sqlite3Fts5StorageRename (fts5_storage.c) handle %_content only for content=normal, so DROP TABLE leaves <name>_content behind and ALTER TABLE RENAME leaves it under the old name (then INSERT 'database disk image is malformed', SELECT 'no such table: main.<new>_content'). Since contentless_unindexed= (3.50.2 to trunk); found while reviewing the locale=1 fix

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-21; between trunk 3769f60be38b (16:05) and fa0247a431bd (16:56), with a change of its own (our fix.diff no longer applies: build-fixed.sh skipped it); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: fa0247a431bd (2026-10-21 16:56): the check prints its expected output on the workspace's trunk CLI

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5vocab-term-range-utf16-order
bugs.summary: fts5vocab in a UTF-16 database: fts5VocabBestIndexMethod takes `term` <, <=, >, >= and ORDER BY term (orderByConsumed) and fts5VocabFilterMethod applies them to the index's UTF-8 terms in memcmp order, which is not the database's UTF-16 BINARY order: a range drops terms between U+0800 and U+FFFF (UTF-16le) or around surrogate pairs (UTF-16be), and ORDER BY term returns UTF-8 order (row, col and instance tables, a range pushed down into a subquery too; never extra rows). fts4aux has the same logic (not in this fix). 3.51.0, 3.54.1 and trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round v2-gaps
bugs.expected:
q1|apple ĳs
q2|apple b ĳs
q3|ĳs apple b
q4|ĳs

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-detail-none-secure-delete-replaced-rowid
bugs.summary: FTS5 detail=none: a rowid deleted and re-inserted in one transaction while secure-delete was off leaves a doclist entry with the delete flag pair 00 00; once secure-delete is on, deleting that rowid makes fts5DoSecureDelete (fts5_index.c) mis-parse the flagged entry: phantom rowids (deleted rowids still match, others appear), checksum mismatches, prefix=1 'corruption found reading blob'. detail=full and column unaffected. 3.51.0 and trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round core-content

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-secure-delete-merge-drops-marker
bugs.summary: FTS5 with secure-delete on: a merge (fts5IndexMergeLevel) writes only the newest duplicate of a term/rowid with its own flag, so a plain entry over a delete marker comes out plain in a non-oldest output (or an incremental merge's trimmed input loses the marker), and a later secure delete of that rowid removes the plain entry and exposes the older one: deleted rows match again, checksum mismatch. All detail modes; in detail=none the fix needs the detail=none secure-delete fix (sqlite-fts5-detail-none-secure-delete-replaced-rowid) too, both apply in either order and the check uses detail=full and column only. 3.46.0 to trunk; found by the independent review of the detail=none bug

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-tokendata-missing-term-dlidx-corrupt
bugs.summary: FTS5 tokendata=1: a query for a term absent from a segment (or present after merge steps) makes fts5SegIterSeekInit take bDlidx from the %_idx row of another page and load a doclist-index that does not exist: 'fts5: corruption found reading blob' on a sound database. 3.46.0 to trunk 185ffd27064b; found in ephyra-sqlite round fts-rtree-2

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-21 02:54; between trunk 185ffd27064b and 3769f60be38b, with a simpler change of its own (the doclist-index is not loaded when the iterator is not on the term's page; our fix-v2.diff no longer applies); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options

bugs.name: sqlite-rtree-update-set-rowid-ignored
bugs.summary: R-Tree: UPDATE .. SET rowid/oid/_rowid_ = N and INSERT INTO r(rowid, ..) ignore the new rowid (rtreeUpdate reads only aData[2], the id column): the row stays, OR REPLACE adds instead of replacing, no conflict error. 3.46.0 to trunk 185ffd27064b; side finding of the geopoly-update-rowid-nochange triage

fixed_in.how: upstream, after our bug-forum report of 2026-10-21 05:32; between trunk 185ffd27064b and 3769f60be38b, with a change of its own (our fix-v2.diff no longer applies); check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-secure-delete-dlidx-walks-next-term
bugs.summary: FTS5 secure-delete: after the last rowids of a term with a doclist-index are removed, fts5SegIterNextFrom jumps to the page the stale doclist-index names and fts5SegIterGotoPage walks past the term boundary into the next term's rowids (`t('a') WHERE rowid >= N` returns rows of another term; integrity-check passes). 3.46.0 to trunk 185ffd27064b; found by the independent review of sqlite-fts5-secure-delete-merge-drops-marker, already fixed upstream before it was reported

fixed_in.how: upstream before we reported it (found 2026-10-21 by our review on 185ffd27064b): fts5SegIterGotoPage gained the same fts5LeafIsTermless check, alongside the tokendata fix, between 185ffd27064b and 3769f60be38b; never open in the registry, recorded for completeness; check-in id not looked up
fixed_in.trunk: 3769f60be38b (2026-10-21 16:05): the check prints its expected output on a CLI with the runner's options (our fix-v2.diff applies too, as a duplicate)

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-near-nomatch-stale-poslist
bugs.summary: fts5ExprNearTest (fts5_expr.c, detail=full) stops at the first NEAR phrase that does not match a row, leaving the earlier phrases with this row's rebuilt position lists and the later ones with an older row's, and sqlite3Fts5ExprPoslist ignores the group's bNomatch: when an OR/NOT sibling matches the row (NEAR(...) OR x, x NOT NEAR(...); NEAR with 2+ phrases and a column filter or a multi-token phrase), highlight()/snippet()/bm25()/ORDER BY rank report stale instances, and snippet() can fail with 'database disk image is malformed' (an offset past the column's end). Integrity checks pass. 3.46.0 to trunk; found by the runner (run 20261021-2000, norec, snippet(vt1, -1, ..) in a materialized CTE). Its fix and sqlite-fts5-and-nomatch-clears-later-row's fix-combined.diff apply in either order
bugs.expected:
q1|1:[h] e d [c],2:p q s t u
q2|[r] h d c

bugs.name: sqlite-drop-constraint-fk-set-default
bugs.summary: ALTER TABLE .. DROP CONSTRAINT of a named foreign key: getConstraint (alter.c) ends the constraint at the first token of its stop set and, for REFERENCES, skips only the table name, so it stops inside the FK clause at the DEFAULT of ON DELETE/UPDATE SET DEFAULT, the NOT of NOT DEFERRABLE, or a MATCH name GENERATED; dropConstraintFunc deletes only up to there: SET DEFAULT and a table-level NOT DEFERRABLE fail with 'error in table c after drop constraint', a column NOT DEFERRABLE stays behind and applies to the table's previous FK (a deferred FK becomes immediate), MATCH generated leaves a new column 'generated' (table FK) or a declared type (column FK). 3.54.0 (FK constraints droppable since then) to trunk; found while extending the generator to DROP CONSTRAINT in ephyra-sqlite round constraints-json (reading getConstraint). Its fix and sqlite-drop-not-null-not-deferrable's touch the same functions and apply in either order
bugs.expected:
q1|CREATE TABLE c1(x, y)
q2|CREATE TABLE c2(w REFERENCES p DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, x, y)
q3|CREATE TABLE c3(x, y)
q5|CREATE TABLE c5(x, y)

bugs.name: sqlite-drop-not-null-not-deferrable
bugs.summary: ALTER TABLE .. ALTER COLUMN .. DROP NOT NULL: dropConstraintFunc (alter.c) takes the column's first NOT (or a named constraint starting with NOT) for the NOT NULL without checking NULL follows, so it removes NOT DEFERRABLE instead and reports success with the column still NOT NULL; and getConstraint does not stop at DEFERRABLE, so removing a NOT NULL (DROP/SET NOT NULL) or a named CHECK/NOT NULL (DROP CONSTRAINT) also removes a following DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, which belongs to the column's FK: the FK silently becomes immediate. 3.53.2, 3.53.4, 3.54.0 and trunk (no DROP NOT NULL before 3.53); split out of sqlite-drop-constraint-fk-set-default by its independent review. Both fixes apply in either order
bugs.expected:
q1|CREATE TABLE c1(x REFERENCES p NOT DEFERRABLE, y)
q2|CREATE TABLE c2(x REFERENCES p DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, y)
q3|CREATE TABLE c3(x REFERENCES p DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, y)
q4|CREATE TABLE c4(x REFERENCES p DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED NOT NULL, y)

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-and-nomatch-clears-later-row
bugs.summary: fts5ExprNodeTest_AND (fts5_expr.c) zeroes every descendant's position list when a non-root AND fails on a row because an operand has the terms without matching (phrase, NEAR group, column filter), though a phrase under an OR or a NOT's right side below it may already sit on a later row the query returns: there highlight()/snippet()/bm25()/ORDER BY rank (detail=full) miss that phrase's instances. The fix is fix-combined.diff, which also fixes sqlite-fts5-not-eof-rhs-instances (no entry of its own: a NOT whose left side is at EOF from the first row never runs fts5ExprNodeTest_NOT, so its right side reports instances, `g OR (zz NOT b)` highlights b); check-combined.sql checks both (q1-q2 AND, q3-q4 NOT). Integrity checks pass. 3.46.0 to trunk; found by the independent review's randomized differential of the sqlite-fts5-near-nomatch-stale-poslist fix, which applies with it in either order

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5vocab-rowid-or-right-join
bugs.summary: fts5vocab (fts5_vocab.c): fts5VocabResetCursor restarts the rowid at 0 on every xFilter, and a scan for term = ? / term >= ? starts at that term, so the same row has different rowids in different scans; the core's MULTI-INDEX OR dedup (OP_RowSetTest) and RIGHT/FULL JOIN unmatched-row tracking key on the rowid: `term = 'banana' OR term < 'c'` returns banana twice and loses apple, `t RIGHT JOIN v` loses rows and reports matched ones as unmatched. Row, col and instance tables, every detail mode (fts4aux has the same bug, not in this fix). 3.46.0 to trunk; found by the runner (run 20261021-2138, cte oracle, cte-materialized, w8-10232). Its fix and sqlite-fts5vocab-term-range-utf16-order's apply in either order

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5-trigram-like-unindexed
bugs.summary: FTS5 trigram tokenizer: LIKE/GLOB on an UNINDEXED column return no rows: fts5BestIndexMethod (fts5_main.c) passes the pattern to xFilter as L<col>/G<col> without checking abUnindexed, and the pattern expression on a column with no tokens matches nothing (a literal run of 3+ characters; LIKE with case_sensitive 0, GLOB either; external content, contentless_unindexed, detail=none, locale=1 too; `+b LIKE p` is right). 3.46.0 to trunk (probably since 3.34.0's trigram pattern pushdown); found by the runner (run 20261022-0005, norec, gen+wal w13-51224)

bugs.name: sqlite-wr-multi-or-seekscan
bugs.summary: A MULTI-INDEX OR on a WITHOUT ROWID table misses rows when an OR-term's IN on the second key column is coded with OP_SeekScan (stat1 says the = prefix matches few rows): wherecode.c emits the OP_NullRow that makes SeekScan's first iteration seek only for iLevel>0, but OR sub-loops are coded at level 0 and share the never-reopened table cursor, which an earlier OR-term or outer iteration left past the IN's keys, so SeekScan concludes no match (`a = 2 OR (a = 1 AND b IN (1, 2))` loses (1,1)). Rowid tables escape (OP_ReopenIdx). 3.35.0 to trunk (since OP_SeekScan, 4a43430fd23f8835); found by the NoREC oracle (candidate sqlite-semantic-depth/sqlite-wr-multi-or-in-misses-row)

bugs.name: sqlite-rename-column-ipk-unique
bugs.summary: ALTER TABLE .. RENAME COLUMN of a single-column INTEGER PRIMARY KEY named in a UNIQUE table constraint fails with 'error in table t after rename: no such column: c' (rolled back): the UNIQUE's column resolved to iColumn -1 or the column index depending on whether it came after or before the PRIMARY KEY clause, and renameColumnExprCb (alter.c) matches only one of them (WITHOUT ROWID with UNIQUE after the key; rowid table with UNIQUE before it). Error only, no wrong schema. 3.25.0 to trunk; found in ephyra-sqlite round xfer-grammar (seed 720)
bugs.expected:
q1|CREATE TABLE t1(z INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(z), UNIQUE(z)) WITHOUT ROWID
q2|CREATE TABLE t2(z INTEGER, d, UNIQUE(d, z), PRIMARY KEY(z))

bugs.name: sqlite-partition-groupby-equal-values-pushdown
bugs.summary: A WHERE term on a subquery with a window function (pushDownWindowCheck, select.c) or a HAVING term (havingToWhere) that uses only PARTITION BY / GROUP BY expressions is moved below the window/aggregate by sqlite3ExprIsConstantOrGroupBy (expr.c), which treats such terms as constant per partition/group; but values that compare equal (integer 1 and real 1.0) can be told apart (typeof, ||), so single rows are removed from a partition/group and sum() OVER (PARTITION BY a) / sum() GROUP BY a give 10 instead of 30. Wrong result on trunk 4fee54f1d687 and every trunk CLI on the host back to 03f699544e6b

bugs.name: sqlite-full-join-using-column-affinity
bugs.summary: The USING column of a FULL JOIN whose left column is REAL reads back as REAL through a materialized subquery, CTE, DISTINCT subquery or window query: a right-only row's integer 9007199254740993 becomes 9007199254740992.0 (sqlite3SubqueryColumnTypes gives the SQLITE_AFF_DEFER coalesce() the left column's REAL affinity, so the reader adds OP_RealAffinity)

bugs.name: sqlite-fts5vocab-without-rowid-pk-null-isnull
bugs.summary: fts5vocab tables declared WITHOUT ROWID with PRIMARY KEY(term, col...) get implicit NOT NULL PK columns, so WHERE col/offset IS NULL is folded to false although the vtab returns NULL for them (detail=none/column).

bugs.name: sqlite-like-opt-counter-uninit-left-join
bugs.summary: Since check-in 08e979525ff1 (the fix for our 74bf8db543) the LIKE optimization loop counter is set after the == terms; an == term that is NULL jumps past it, and a LEFT JOIN's NULL row re-enters the loop body and reaches OP_DecrJumpZero on the uninitialized counter: debug builds assert memIsValid, release builds may restart the LIKE loop with uncomputed key registers (runner worker SIGSEGV in vdbeRecordCompareString via sqlite3BtreeIndexMoveto, run 20261027-0705). Needs a GLOB prefix or case-sensitive LIKE and an outer join. Check: the fixed build's bytecode sets the counter (Integer 0) before the IsNull.
